articles.title: Our AI wrote 125 blog posts. A second AI found 4,334 mistakes in them.
articles.excerpt: The first four blog posts our system wrote all scored 100 out of 100 on our own SEO check. Every one of them still had three to six mistakes in it. That check counts things. Keyword in the title, leng…
articles.body: The first four blog posts our system wrote all scored 100 out of 100 on our own SEO check. Every one of them still had three to six mistakes in it. That check counts things. Keyword in the title, length of the intro, number of links, whether there's an FAQ. It never reads a sentence. So a post can tick every box and still say that four tasks add up to 45 hours when they add up to 35. I'm Bauke, and together with Stijn I run Chef AI, a small agency in Amsterdam that automates back office work for Dutch SMBs. Since early October an AI writes the blogs on our site, in Dutch, from keyword research to a draft in our CMS. I read every draft and I publish them myself. But I didn't want to be the one who finds the wrong sums. So we added a second reader.
articles.author: Bauke ten Have

articles.title: How we made a 185-page Flutter web app readable by Google and AI crawlers
articles.excerpt: Flutter web draws your app onto a canvas. That is great for users and terrible for crawlers: a fresh flutter build web hands Google a page with almost no text, no headings and the same title on every…
articles.body: Flutter web draws your app onto a canvas. That is great for users and terrible for crawlers: a fresh flutter build web hands Google a page with almost no text, no headings and the same title on every route. We run TypeorDrop , a free file-tools site (PDF, Word, image, audio and video converters) built entirely in Flutter web. It has 185 public URLs. This is how we made every one of them readable without server-side rendering, headless Chrome, or changing a single widget, and what crawlers actually did afterwards. The generic tooling is open source: nexina/flutter-web-seo (MIT, Python, no dependencies).
articles.author: Rakibul Hasan

articles.body: I just published a preprint describing TA TA, an autonomous agent system I built over four years and publicly launched in October 2026. Paper: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24123263 (Zenodo preprint, CC BY 4.0) Live system: https://www.aiagentcoo.com The problem Autonomous agents are moving from tools humans operate to economic actors that transact with each other. When a buying agent purchases inference, data, or a service from a service agent, three questions become unavoidable: Whose is it? If an agent earns or holds an asset, who owns it? Who approved it? Which operations may an agent perform autonomously, and which require a human? Where is the receipt? Can every action be reconstructed after the fact?

articles.title: Kagelin v1.52.0: Building Universal Migration & Zero-Knowledge Data Portability
articles.excerpt: Moving between productivity apps usually hurts. Proprietary formats, lost hierarchies, missing checklists, and vendor lock-in keep users tethered to legacy tools. Kagelin v1.52.0, our goal was simple:…
articles.body: Moving between productivity apps usually hurts. Proprietary formats, lost hierarchies, missing checklists, and vendor lock-in keep users tethered to legacy tools. With Kagelin v1.52.0 , our goal was simple: true data portability without compromising client-side privacy. Here is an architectural walkthrough of how we built universal importers for Microsoft To Do, Google Tasks, and TickTick, introduced bitmask notification controls, and decoupled task schedules from deadlines. 1. Zero-Knowledge Client-Side Migration Most migration workflows route your raw data or credentials through a backend parser. Because Kagelin operates under a local-first, privacy-first model , migrations run entirely in the browser.
articles.author: Achyuth S

articles.title: Vibe Coding Photoshot Retouch, Part 1 — From a Photo to Editable Layers
articles.excerpt: Say a retouch removes a blemish and softens the dark area under an eye. The blemish looks better, but you want some of the original shadow back. If each correction comes back on its own layer, you can…
articles.body: Say a retouch removes a blemish and softens the dark area under an eye. The blemish looks better, but you want some of the original shadow back. If each correction comes back on its own layer, you can fade just the shadow correction. A layer is like a transparent sheet over the photo, and a mask controls how much of that sheet shows in each spot. What we’re building in 24 parts Photoshot Retouch is a photo-retouching tool for a web editor and Adobe Photoshop. In this vibe coding series I describe the behavior I want, build it with AI assistance, and check that behavior on a small example before moving on. Parts 1–4 start with a tiny image and build the first masked PNG, face analysis, and layer output.
articles.author: 김기선

articles.title: Accuracy First, Rarity Second: The Closed Answer List Behind a Rare-Answer Warm-Up
articles.excerpt: If you build a game where the rarest correct answer wins, you quickly find out that "correct" is the hard part. Rarity is just counting. Deciding what counts as a valid answer in the first place is wh…
articles.body: If you build a game where the rarest correct answer wins, you quickly find out that "correct" is the hard part. Rarity is just counting. Deciding what counts as a valid answer in the first place is where most of the design work lives, and it is the part players notice the moment you get it wrong. I run an unofficial Krillion Roblox fan guide with a small browser warm-up on it. To be clear up front: it is a fan page, not the game. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Krillion or Roblox Corporation, and I am not the Krillion developer. The real game is Krillion [Official] – Guess the Rarest Answer on Roblox, and there is also a browser version at krillion.io.

articles.title: Set Up a WordPress Staging-to-Production Workflow with Git
articles.excerpt: We've all done it. You change one line of CSS directly on the live site, hit save, and the homepage turns into modern art. The fix is boring and it works: write and test your changes on a staging copy…
articles.body: We've all done it. You change one line of CSS directly on the live site, hit save, and the homepage turns into modern art. The fix is boring and it works: write and test your changes on a staging copy of the site, keep your code in Git, and push to production only when everything looks right. This guide sets that up in about 30 minutes. No paid plugins, no deployment platform to learn. The idea in one minute Two sites, two branches, one rule. Site URL Git branch Staging staging.example.com staging Production example.com main The rule: code moves up (local → staging → production). Content moves down (production → staging). Git tracks your theme (or custom plugin). It does not track your database, your uploads, or wp-config.php .
articles.author: Muhammad Usman

articles.title: Cairn AI Agents Found a Zero-Day on Their Own: What Autonomous Vulnerability Discovery Means for Security Infrastructure
articles.excerpt: AWS Security just documented the first known case of offensive AI agents discovering a zero-day vulnerability without human direction. Chinese-nexus threat actors deployed Cairn AI agents that perform…
articles.body: AWS Security just documented the first known case of offensive AI agents discovering a zero-day vulnerability without human direction. Chinese-nexus threat actors deployed Cairn AI agents that performed reconnaissance, fuzzing, and exploitation autonomously. No human-in-the-loop. No manual triage. The agents found the vulnerability, validated it, and prepared exploitation paths on their own. This is not agent-assisted hacking. This is fully autonomous offensive security research running in production environments. The defensive implications are immediate: your SOC is built to detect human attackers who sleep, make mistakes, and operate at human speed. Autonomous agents iterate faster, run 24/7, and generate behavioral patterns that do not match existing detection rules.

articles.title: Will astronauts farm on the moon? Scientists successfully grow potatoes in simulated lunar dust

articles.body: It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal.

articles.title: NASA Awards Contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program
articles.excerpt: NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) in…
articles.body: Credit: NASA NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites. The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from Nov. 23 through April 1, 2042. The work will take place at the awardee’s facility. Under the contract, Northrop Grumman will provide the design, development, production, testing, and mission support for three SMBA instruments, the next generation of low Earth orbit microwave sounders.
